Package com.github.workerframework.queues.rabbit

Class RabbitWorkerQueue

java.lang.Object
com.github.workerframework.queues.rabbit.RabbitWorkerQueue
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.github.cafapi.common.api.HealthReporter, ManagedWorkerQueue, WorkerQueue
public final class RabbitWorkerQueue extends Object implements ManagedWorkerQueue
This implementation uses a separate thread for a consumer and producer, each with their own Channel. These threads handle operations via a BlockingQueue of Event objects. In all scenarios where the tasks triggered by the message take significantly longer than the handling of the messages themselves (which should hopefully be true of all microservices), this implementation should work. This implementation has three routing keys, assumed to be on a direct exchange (hence effectively being queue names). There is the input queue to receive messages from, the retry queue (which may be the input queue) where redelivered messages get republished to, and the rejected queue which is where messages that could not be handled are put. There are an unlimited number of possible output queues as defined by the Worker's response. All published messages use RabbitMQ confirmations.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start(TaskCallback callback) throws QueueException
      Open queues to start accepting tasks and results. Create a RabbitMQ connection, and separate incoming and outgoing channels. The connection and channels will attempt to re-establish should they drop. Declare the queues on the appropriate channels and kick off the publisher and consumer threads to handle messages. Since this code uses publisher confirms, it is important currently to declare the publisher channel before the consumer channel, otherwise during a connection drop scenario, the client can report the publish sequence number for the "old" channel before recovering it.
      Specified by:
      start in interface ManagedWorkerQueue
      Parameters:
      callback - the callback to use when registering or aborting tasks
      Throws:
      QueueException - if the queue cannot be started

    • shutdownIncoming

      public void shutdownIncoming()
      Halt the incoming queue so that no more tasks are picked up. The incoming queues will all be cancelled so the consumer will fall back to idle.
      Specified by:

    • disconnectIncoming

      public void disconnectIncoming()
      Disconnects the incoming queue so that no more tasks are consumed. This method can be used to stop a worker consuming messages from it's input queue. This is useful in, (for example), an instance where a worker's health check has failed. The worker is disconnected from the incoming channel and the consumerTag removed from the list of consumerTags.
      Specified by:
      disconnectIncoming in interface ManagedWorkerQueue

    • reconnectIncoming

      public void reconnectIncoming()
      Reconnects the incoming queue so tasks consumption can resume. This method can be used to reconnect a worker to it's input queue therefore allowing to resume consuming messages. This is useful in, (for example), an instance where a worker's health check indicates the worker has become healthy again and should resume consuming messages. The worker is reconnected to the incoming channel and the returned consumerTag added to the list of consumerTags.
      Specified by:
      reconnectIncoming in interface ManagedWorkerQueue
